title: Known issue: Streamed responses ending early (SSE disconnect / missing [DONE] / truncated output)
author: Avery Johnson
body:
## Summary
Some customers may report that **streamed** responses (chat/completions) **end early**, producing **partial/truncated output**. Common customer phrasing includes:
- "SSE disconnect" / "SSE closes early"
- "the stream just stops" / "stream cut off"
- "missing [DONE]"
- "connection closed" (often from a proxy or client library)
- "we get an EOF and the message is incomplete"

## Affected surfaces
- OpenAI-compatible: `/v1/chat/completions` with `stream=true`
- SDKs: Python/TypeScript/Go (behavior varies; some treat disconnect as EOF without an explicit error)

## Root cause (as observed in Nov 2025 incident)
When the model path introduces a long pause (e.g., tool selection or long prefill), there can be **no bytes flushed** to the client for ~2040s. The API gateway (Envoy) may enforce a **downstream idle timeout** (commonly 30s), closing the connection.

## How to confirm
1) Look for request traces with a large gap between streamed deltas
2) In gateway logs, confirm downstream close/idle timeout
3) Customer symptom: stream terminates without terminal marker; response content is partial

## Workarounds (customer-facing)
- Temporarily disable streaming for longest responses
- Increase customer-side proxy read/idle timeouts (if they have a proxy/load balancer)
- Reduce prompt/response size; split long generations
- Retry on incomplete output (not ideal but mitigates impact)

## Fix
Engineering fix is to **send periodic keep-alive bytes** (heartbeat/flush) on streaming responses when token deltas are not emitted for N seconds.

## Escalation guidance
Escalate to Eng if:
- More than ~1% of streaming calls are affected
- Customer is Dedicated/Enterprise and impact is user-visible
- Customer reports missing terminal event or consistent truncation
